headline: Gunshots fired at singer Asif Akbar's car in Dhaka
summary: The vehicle was targeted in Moghbazar early Saturday; the singer was not inside the car during the attack.
details: A car belonging to singer Asif Akbar was targeted by gunfire in Dhaka's Moghbazar area early Saturday morning.
The incident took place outside the Bishal Centre shopping complex, according to Hatirjheel Police Station chief Asaduzzaman.
Police confirmed that Asif Akbar was not inside the vehicle at the time of the shooting, and no casualties were reported.
Authorities are currently investigating the motive behind the attack and working to identify the suspects involved.
caption:
Gunshots fired at singer Asif Akbar's car in Dhaka. No one was injured as the singer was not inside the vehicle.

A car belonging to singer Asif Akbar was targeted by gunfire in Dhaka's Moghbazar area early Saturday morning.

The incident took place outside the Bishal Centre shopping complex, according to Hatirjheel Police Station chief Asaduzzaman.

Police confirmed that Asif Akbar was not inside the vehicle at the time of the shooting, and no casualties were reported.

Authorities are currently investigating the motive behind the attack and working to identify the suspects involved.

headline: 7 killed as gunmen attack church in Jordan during funeral
summary: Authorities describe the shooting at Hamoud Church in Karak as a terrorist act by extremists, leaving 40 people wounded.
details: Seven people were killed on Friday when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at the Hamoud Church in Jordan's Karak governorate.
According to the country's health minister, 40 people were wounded in the attack. Major General Abdallah al-Maaytah stated that most of the injured are still receiving treatment.
Security camera footage showed three attackers firing from a sidewalk and hiding behind trees and a wall before rushing the church entrance.
Interior Minister Mazin Al Farrayeh described the perpetrators as extremists, though it is not yet clear if they are linked to any known groups.
Jordan's King Abdullah visited Karak and vowed that the perpetrators would be punished with an iron fist, emphasizing national unity against terrorism.
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and US ambassador Mike Waltz condemned the violence, calling attacks on places of worship unacceptable.
Christians are a minority in Jordan, a country that has repeatedly foiled Islamist militant attacks in recent years.
caption:
7 dead and 40 wounded after gunmen storm a church funeral in Jordan. Authorities call it a 'terrorist act'.

Seven people were killed on Friday when gunmen opened fire during a funeral at the Hamoud Church in Jordan's Karak governorate.

According to the country's health minister, 40 people were wounded in the attack. Major General Abdallah al-Maaytah stated that most of the injured are still receiving treatment.

Security camera footage showed three attackers firing from a sidewalk and hiding behind trees and a wall before rushing the church entrance.

Interior Minister Mazin Al Farrayeh described the perpetrators as extremists, though it is not yet clear if they are linked to any known groups.

Jordan's King Abdullah visited Karak and vowed that the perpetrators would be punished with an iron fist, emphasizing national unity against terrorism.

United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and US ambassador Mike Waltz condemned the violence, calling attacks on places of worship unacceptable.

Christians are a minority in Jordan, a country that has repeatedly foiled Islamist militant attacks in recent years.
